title: Orthogonal Nonnegative Matrix Tri-Factorizations for Clustering
venue: ACM SIGKDD International Conference on Knowledge Discovery and Data Mining (KDD)

citations.claim: Ding et al. showed that nonnegative matrix factorization with an orthogonality constraint on one factor (G^T G = I) is equivalent to K-means clustering.

Ding et al. introduced orthogonal nonnegative matrix tri-factorization X = FSG^T with bi-orthogonality constraints (F^T F = I, G^T G = I), where the intermediate factor S absorbs scale differences and enables simultaneous row and column clustering.
Orthogonality constraints in NMF provide uniqueness of the solution up to permutation, eliminating the rotational ambiguity present in unconstrained NMF.

Ding et al. proved that unconstrained 3-factor NMF (X = FSG^T) is equivalent to unconstrained 2-factor NMF, but constrained 3-factor NMF with orthogonality brings genuinely new properties such as rigorous clustering interpretation.
Ding et al. provided multiplicative update rules for orthogonal NMF and proved their convergence using auxiliary function methods and matrix inequalities.

do_not_claim: Ding et al. applied orthogonal NMF to signal processing or baseline correction
Ding et al. proposed algorithm unrolling or deep learning approaches
Ding et al. addressed sparse signal decomposition in the sense of y = x + f + n
